{"type":"text","timestamp":1794623406668,"sessionID":"ses_e281e371bffeExbO0IM0bDTnRp","part":{"id":"prt_1d7e40238001vZ9zV70sgSLbQc","messageID":"msg_1d7e3e3e8001CKhF4nljBQSsg9","sessionID":"ses_e281e371bffeExbO0IM0bDTnRp","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover sampled 3 targets on time, worth 6 points, and finished alive at base with about 2.4 battery left. Mission targets were worth 13 in total, so the expected score is about 6/13 ≈ 0.46.\n\n**Sampled on time:** t1 (2), t5 (2) and t2 (2). From the position fixes at ticks 31–47, the rover sat at about (20.0, 20.0), well inside the 0.75 m base radius. I can't confirm the scored result, since it's computed from the rover's true position, but the fixes put it there.\n\n**Missed:**\n- **t4 (1):** I drove past it by about 1 m. I had planned on about 30% slip on sand, but the real figure was closer to 15–20%, and the sample at tick 16 failed.\n- **d2 (3):** This target appeared mid-mission and had the highest value. Because of the 3-tick delay, the drives toward it were queued before I had a usable position fix. A heading error of about −3° left the rover about 0.9 m short, and the sample at tick 22 (its deadline) failed.\n- **d1 (2) and t3 (1):** I skipped these to save battery. After d2 failed, the battery could cover only one more target plus the drive home without risking dying, which scores zero. I chose t2 because it was on the way back.\n\nThe biggest mistake was queuing several drives and the sample in one go, with no chance to correct in between.
